## Chapter 5B Evidence Router — IMF 2022 Article IV (MAC-010)

**Scope:** 10 lenses (5B.1–5B.10) · 10 chunks supplied (U0001–U0010)

---

### Routing Decisions

| chunk_id | Locator | Decision | Applicable Lens(es) | Exclusion Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **U0001** | page 1 | **EXCLUDE** | — | Cover page, copyright notice, document inventory. No policy content, measured outcome, cost, distributional result, implementation finding, method, qualification, attribution fact, or contrary finding. |
| **U0002** | page 2 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9 | Contains concrete policy facts: fiscal deficit of 3.8% GDP with broadly neutral stance; untargeted subsidies used to mitigate cost-of-living; gross debt at ~56% GDP; policy rate at 9.25% in series of hikes; current account deficit of 0.4% GDP. Directors' assessment language on "largely untargeted subsidies" is a distributional/incidence finding relevant to 5B.8 and a targeting effectiveness finding relevant to 5B.9. |
| **U0003** | page 3 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.5, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9 | Multiple concrete findings: retail fuel price smoothing "had a sizable cost on the budget" (5B.3, 5B.6 cost fact); recommendation to shift toward "more targeted support" (5B.8 distributional; 5B.9 targeting); Directors urging "broaden the supply side policy agenda for higher and more inclusive growth" with specific items — corruption/rule of law, human capital, infrastructure bottlenecks, labor/product market rigidities, financial deepening (5B.1 policy agenda; 5B.6 budget quality). Explicit recommendation for "gradual increase in productive spending, financed by tax reforms" (5B.6, 5B.3). |
| **U0004** | page 4 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.10 | Selected economic indicators table — provides quantified baseline for GDP growth (2.1% 2022 → 1.2% 2023), inflation (7.4%→8.5%→4.8%), fiscal balance (−3.8% GDP), gross debt (57.6%→56.2%→57.7% GDP). These are measured outcomes for trajectory assessment (5B.10) and fiscal rule performance (5B.3, 5B.6). Footnotes provide methodology for poverty measurement (social deprivation index). |
| **U0005** | page 5 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.9 | Staff's own policy recommendations section — concrete actions: "moving towards more market-based fuel pricing would create room for providing targeted income support to vulnerable households" (5B.8 distribution; 5B.9 targeting); "permanent increase in productive spending, financed by tax reform" (5B.6; 5B.3); "raise the policy rate further to a firmly restrictive level" (5B.3); financial sector "strengthening capacity of regulatory agencies," "consolidated supervision," "cyber risk regulation," "upgrading macroprudential toolkit" (5B.4 fair regulation, 5B.5 anti-corruption/best practice); structural priorities including rule of law, governance, labor market formality, competition in energy sector (5B.1, 5B.4). This is the IMF's own evidence on policy quality. |
| **U0006** | page 6 | **EXCLUDE** | — | Mission team composition and full Table of Contents. Lists section headings (Context, Recent Developments, Outlook, Policy Discussions, etc.) but contains no findings, data, policy content, or evaluations. Adjacent context only. |
| **U0007** | page 7 | **EXCLUDE** | — | Continuation of Table of Contents — list of boxes, figures, tables, and annexes. No substantive content. Adjacent context only. |
| **U0008** | page 8 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.4, 5B.7, 5B.10 | Context section with specific findings: "investment weakened in the pandemic downturn, reinforcing the impact of increased policy uncertainty in some sectors in recent years" (5B.1 investment climate; 5B.10 trajectory); "long-standing problems of low growth, weak productivity, and high inequality" with specific named obstacles: "rule of law, corruption, and crime issues; regional disparities; and weak outcomes in education and health" (5B.1 policy agenda; 5B.4 regulatory quality; 5B.7 information/reform orientation). Figure on manufacturing exports with quantified data points. |
| **U0009** | page 9 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.8, 5B.9 | Rich empirical content: fuel subsidies increased in 2022 to moderate energy price inflation (5B.3 fiscal rule; 5B.9 shock response); food inflation at 14.1% in August, exceeding target for a decade, accounting for "over 50 percent of the increase in headline inflation above target" (5B.8 distributional incidence — food price burden on lower-income households); core inflation rose to 8.1% as "price pressures have broadened" (5B.7 information quality about inflation incidence); chart showing counterfactual fuel prices with no subsidies vs actual (methodology for measuring subsidy impact). |
| **U0010** | page 10 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.2, 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Capacity utilization data (manufacturing sector, percentage points); unemployment/underemployment rates by period — quantified measured outcomes for 5B.6 (admin capacity, job creation) and 5B.10 trajectory; sector-level output comparison (2022Q1 vs 2019 average) for construction, finance, temporary services, etc. — evidence of differentiated sectoral performance bearing on budget quality and distributional effects. Monetary policy acceleration: "25 bp hikes initially, then 50 and 75 bp hikes when inflation became broad-based" — operational detail on policy process (5B.2 central bank independence context; 5B.3 monetary rules). |

### Audit Trail — Exclusion Justifications

- **U0001 (EXCLUDE):** Cover page, document inventory, copyright. Purely administrative.
- **U0006 (EXCLUDE):** Mission team roster and section heading list. No analytical content.
- **U0007 (EXCLUDE):** Continuation of Table of Contents — list of boxes, figures, tables, annexes. No findings, no data, no policy content. Adjacent structural context only.
